traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md are satisfied.
- Core Functionality: The `valid-req-reference` rule, together with its helpers, parses referenced story files, caches discovered requirement IDs, and verifies that every @req and @supports requirement ID exists in the corresponding story file. Tests explicitly cover both matching and missing requirement cases. - Quality Standards: Validation is format- and structure-agnostic by design via a global `REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+` regex over the entire markdown file. Fixtures and tests demonstrate handling of plain-text IDs, bullet lists, and multi-story scenarios; the same mechanism naturally supports IDs in numbered lists, checkboxes, and different sections. - Integration: The rule is wired into src/index.ts, participates in the recommended and strict presets, and reuses existing annotation and file validation patterns. Integration tests and the full Jest run confirm it coexists correctly with all other rules. - User Experience: Error messages `reqMissing` and `invalidPath` are specific and include both the requirement ID and story path. Tests assert these messages and data fields, and docs explain the behavior and examples. - Error Handling: Story file read/parsing errors and unsafe paths are handled via try/catch and explicit path validation, resulting in controlled ESLint diagnostics instead of crashes. Tests cover invalid paths, and the implementation degrades gracefully to empty requirement sets. - Documentation: Both internal rule docs (docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md) and user-facing API docs (user-docs/api-reference.md) describe deep requirement validation behavior and how to use the rule, with examples of supported formats and error scenarios.
Therefore, this story is fully implemented and verified: status PASSED.
